meeting_header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Polaris - Head of Platform), Tom Vasquez (Polaris - Security Lead), Elena Park (Polaris - Legal)
summary: Discovery focused on key residency and encryption controls; Polaris evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for card-processing PII workloads. Main concerns: KMS/key escrow, egress logs, auditability, and contract-level guarantees for region locking. Agreed to share compliance artifacts and run a technical deep dive for network/firewall design.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
SOC 2 / HIPAA evidence and contractual SLAs
transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Okay, um, thanks everyone for joining. quick intro — i'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Liam, our solutions engineer. Can you introduce yourselves?
00:12 - Aisha: Hi, Aisha Rahman, Head of Platform at Polaris. We've got Tom from Security and Elena from Legal on for questions.
00:20 - Tom: Yep, Tom Vasquez.
00:23 - Liam: Great. Quick agenda — residency, encryption, logs, and then next steps. We can go deep on any area you want.
00:34 - Elena: Thanks. We're specifically trying to map out where keys live and what's contractually possible. We have cardholder data flows that currently must remain in eu-west.
00:44 - Maya: Understood. Just to set context: Redwood offers hosted (our cloud), dedicated reserved capacity in regional clusters, and private (VPC or on-prem) where control plane can be isolated. For keys we do KMS integrations and can support customer-managed keys with HSM-backed KMS.
01:05 - Aisha: When you say customer-managed, is that bring-your-own key into your cloud KMS, or do we keep keys entirely in our HSM?
01:12 - Liam: Good question. We have two common patterns — BYOK in your cloud KMS (e.g., AWS KMS in your account with a key policy that restricts Redwood's control plane) or a private deployment where the KMS/HSM sits inside your VPC/on-prem and Redwood's inference nodes talk to it over private networking.
01:34 - Tom: For us, we need to ensure keys never leave our control. The legal team will insist on key escrow provisions being disabled. Is that possible?
01:42 - Maya: We can support no-escrow with private deployments. For hosted there's typically a shared control plane and that complicates no-escrow guarantees. With Dedicated there's an option to bring KMS into your cloud project and we can restrict access via IAM and mutual TLS.
02:05 - Elena: How about the metadata and logs — audit trails, model inputs — can those be region-locked?
02:13 - Liam: Audit logs for control plane ops can be configured to ship to your logging endpoints in region. There is sometimes confusion: application-level request logs (the actual prompts) are handled depending on hosting mode — hosted retains short-lived logs for safety, dedicated can forward logs to your storage, private can be fully in your environment.
02:35 - Aisha: So in Hosted, do you ever store prompts outside eu-west temporarily for routing or cache warmup?
02:42 - Maya: We try not to. In practice, smart routing can route to nearby regions for latency; however we have a region pinning option for customers with strict residency. We'll add that to the docs.
02:58 - Tom: Next, we've got a requirement around redaction — we must never persist raw PAN numbers in logs even transiently. Does Redwood do automatic redaction or masking?
03:08 - Liam: We have tokenization/redaction pipelines as an option. For Hosted customers, you can enable request-level redaction; that creates an event with tokens only. For Dedicated/Private, redaction is typically done on your side before it hits the runtime or as a pre-hook in the private control plane.
03:30 - Elena: And about retention — regulator wants 7 years for some audit artifacts; for others maybe shorter. Can retention be configured per log type?
03:38 - Liam: Yes — control plane logs, access logs, and request logs are independent. In Dedicated we can configure retention and export to your S3/GCS in eu-west. In Hosted there's a max retention window publicly documented but we can discuss enterprise retention add-ons.
03:55 - Speaker 1: (mumble) also want to check encryption in transit.
04:00 - Maya: All traffic to our runtime uses TLS 1.2+ and mTLS for private endpoints. For private deployments we recommend VPC peering or private link equivalents.
04:14 - Aisha: About contractual SLAs — we need a clause to guarantee region lock and indemnity if data is moved incorrectly.
04:22 - Elena: Plus audit rights: can we run audits or get attestation logs?
04:27 - Liam: We provide SOC 2 reports and can enable audit hooks that stream events to your SIEM. For Private, you have direct access to raw logs. For Dedicated, we can arrange log exports and an attestation process.
04:45 - Tom: Any background on key rotation — we need a 90-day rotation cadence and proof of rotation.
04:51 - Maya: We support rotation policies at the KMS layer. If you control KMS, you control rotation and can provide rotation proof. If Redwood manages keys, we publish rotation events to the audit logs.
05:06 - Aisha: Okay. Can we talk about threat model? what if an operator in your control plane misconfigures and routes requests to another region?
05:15 - Liam: Good point. We have guardrails: region pinning, automated routing policies, and change control with review. For Dedicated we can also enable dedicated network paths and restrict admin actions via MFA+RBAC.
05:30 - Maya: quick note — there might be some minor transcription errors in this call, sorry if names get munged.
05:36 - Aisha: (laughs) no worries.
06:00 - Maya: can you describe the pilot you have in mind? size, inputs, and success metrics?
06:07 - Aisha: Pilot would be 1k reqs/hour burst, using a reranking model and some generation for customer emails — mostly PII present, must be processed in eu-west. Success = latency < 250ms p95 and zero PII leakage in logs.
06:25 - Liam: For 1k rps burst we recommend reserved dedicated nodes. We can provide cost estimate based on quantized models. We'll run a quick calc post-call.
06:36 - Tom: Also we need a playbook for incident response and notification windows; legal wants 72-hour SLA for suspected exposure.
06:44 - Elena: And retention of incident logs for investigation.
06:47 - Liam: We can provide an IR playbook plus the timeline. For private deployments you own the logs so retention is controlled by your policy.
07:00 - Speaker 2: what's the path if we need on-prem eventually?
07:05 - Maya: We support an on-prem package — essentially private deployment with customer-managed control plane and optional air-gapped operations. That typically requires an SOW and some professional services.
07:18 - Aisha: Budget question — between dedicated and private what's the rough multiplier?
07:23 - Liam: Private (on-prem) is highest due to infra + support, dedicated reserved is mid, hosted is lowest. We'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing doc.
07:35 - Tom: Can you talk about KMS providers supported?
07:39 - Liam: We integrate with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google Cloud KMS, and can do HSMs via PKCS#11 in private deployments.
07:49 - Elena: Contractistically, we need to ensure there's no key escrow and that Redwood's staff can't decrypt data. Is there a staff access control audit?
07:58 - Maya: We enforce least-privileged admin access, RBAC, and support separation of duties. For Dedicated we can map admin accounts to your SSO and have bridged audit logs.
08:10 - Aisha: about backups — snapshots of model caches could contain prompts, can those be encrypted with customer keys?
08:18 - Liam: Yes, snapshot encryption is supported in Dedicated/Private where you can specify customer-managed keys. In Hosted it's encrypted at rest by our provider keys but we can discuss bring-your-own key for enterprise.
08:33 - Speaker 3: do you offer demonstrable attestation that backups were encrypted with our key?
08:38 - Liam: For private and dedicated yes, we'd provide logs showing key-wrap events; for hosted we can include an attestation that provider KMS was used, but not your key unless BYOK is configured.
08:54 - Elena: ok, this is helpful. Next we need to map out exact legal language around region locking.
09:01 - Maya: We have a region lock addendum template we can share.
09:06 - Aisha: Great. Also, for telemetry — do you collect model metrics that could be considered personal data if combined with prompts?
09:15 - Liam: Metrics are aggregated by default. We treat raw prompts as application data and handle per your retention settings. If you want to avoid telemetry collection entirely we can disable it for your workspace.
09:29 - Tom: Are there any scenarios where Redwood will transfer data to the US for processing?
09:34 - Maya: Only if routing requires it and no region pin exists. For strict customers we set explicit region pinning and routing policies. We also can sign Data Processing Agreements that restrict transfers.
09:49 - Aisha: Will you share the DPAs and SCCs?
09:52 - Maya: Yes, we'll attach the DPA, SCCs, and our certifications.
10:02 - Elena: One more legal nuance — we need to know if logs could be subpoenaed in another jurisdiction.
10:09 - Liam: If logs are stored in your region under your storage account, legal process would have to go through your jurisdiction. If stored in Redwood's systems, we have a data access request process and will notify customers.
10:23 - Maya: (typing) i'll flag the legal team to get you the template clauses.
10:28 - Aisha: Okay let's do a quick dive on a technical path for the pilot — network topology.
10:35 - Liam: Recommended: dedicated VPC peering, private subnets for runtime, NAT for outbound updates only, and private link for control plane ops. We can share a diagram.
10:49 - Tom: On network egress, do you ever route through third-party CDNs?
10:53 - Liam: No for private/dedicated in-region. Hosted uses provider networking but we don't route requests through third-party CDNs.
11:06 - Speaker 1: (inaudible) question on telemetry retention limits?
11:10 - Maya: we'll include the published retention table but as a starting point: hosted 30 days by default, dedicated configurable, private your policy.
11:20 - Elena: We also want a compliance pack showing HIPAA controls mapped to our internal matrix.
11:26 - Maya: we have a HIPAA control mapping doc, we'll share it.
11:30 - Aisha: ok good — one risk: our finance team says dedicated is fine but procurement is worried about ongoing export of logs to third-party S3 if that's in a different region.
11:42 - Liam: That's avoidable — we can set export buckets to be in your tenant and region.
11:48 - Tom: Are there automated redaction SDKs we can run pre-send?
11:52 - Liam: Yes, we provide client-side SDKs with PII detection hooks, and you can apply pre-send redaction or deterministic tokenization.
12:04 - Elena: any blockers for us doing a 2-week pilot starting first week of january?
12:10 - Maya: primary blockers are procurement and providing the data classification diagram. We can schedule the SE deep dive next week to scope infra.
12:20 - Aisha: timeline wise procurement wants contract terms by Jan 10.
12:24 - Maya: we can aim to get the legal and DPA draft over by Dec 24, and pricing by Dec 24 as well.
12:35 - (crosstalk)
12:40 - Liam: i'll run the latency/cost calc and share a spreadsheet.
12:45 - Elena: i'll draft the legal questions list and circulate.
12:50 - Tom: we'll also provide the list of data endpoints that touch PAN.
12:54 - Maya: perfect. quick recap?
13:00 - Maya: recap: Redwood to send pricing + region capacity spreadsheet, SOC2/HIPAA pack, region lock addendum, and schedule SE deep dive. Polaris to send dataflow and classification, legal questions list, and procurement timeline.
13:20 - Aisha: sounds good. thanks all.
13:25 - Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
13:30 - (call ends)

Notes: transcript contains natural disfluencies, occasional speaker mislabels, and abbreviated timestamps for readability. Longer verbatim sections truncated to key exchanges for brevity.
